statement: In ALS, C9orf72-reactive CD4+ T cells are skewed away from an IFNg-dominant response toward IL-4/IL-10, weakening immune surveillance of the C9orf72 antigen.
mechanism: Loss of regulatory restraint on antigen-specific CD4+ T cells shifts their cytokine program from Th1 (IFNg) toward Th2/regulatory (IL-4, IL-10) output in ALS, which this run's hypothesis ties to disease progression.
